title: Rosalind and the Songbook
premise: Marine biologist Zephyrine Brightwater has rebuilt her life around sea turtle conservation on a remote Gulf Coast island, carefully avoiding the past she abandoned in New Orleans. When a freak snowstorm traps her field station with Theo Marchand, the songwriter she loved at twenty-three and never forgave, old wounds reopen alongside an unexpected tenderness. As thaw comes, Zephyrine must choose between a career-saving research grant in Monterey and the man who has finally written the song he should have written a decade ago. She chooses neither path as given: she takes the grant on her own terms and asks Theo to build a life that holds both, ending with the two of them on the island at dawn, counting turtles and new beginnings together.
about_author: Oscar Quintana is a former folk musician turned novelist who spent two years volunteering at coastal wildlife stations before writing his debut. He lives in a small Gulf Coast town, where he still plays Sunday sets at a bar that smells of salt and old pine.

chapters.title: Counting Instead of Feeling
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She conducts her dawn turtle census on Pelican Key, cataloguing nests with practiced detachment while dodging calls from her grant committee. Establishes her rule: measure everything, feel nothing. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the quiet pride of a life rebuilt on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Forecast Says Impossible
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A historic snowstorm — unheard of on the Gulf — closes the ferry and knocks out the island's power. She preps the station for isolation, only to hear a car horn from the causeway. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into alarm as the weather turns biblical.

chapters.title: The Man in the Drift
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She rescues a stranded driver from a snowed-in truck: Theo Marchand, the songwriter who broke her heart ten years ago, now en route to a career-reviving gig in Mobile. Emotional beat: shock curdling into fury as recognition lands.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Bad Weather
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Trapped by the storm, they trade barbed memories of New Orleans — the songbook they wrote together, the night he chose a record deal over her. Flashbacks reveal the misunderstanding neither ever named. Emotional beat: grief wearing anger's clothing.

chapters.title: House Rules for Hostages
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He negotiates fragile truce terms: he'll help with generator and chores, she'll pretend he's a stranger. Small domestic scenes crackle with unresolved history. Emotional beat: wary comedy, the absurdity of intimacy with an enemy.

chapters.title: The Songbook
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Packing away storm supplies, she finds her old notebook of their co-written songs, water-stained but legible. Theo sees it; the room goes silent. Emotional beat: the past made physical, shame and longing colliding.

chapters.title: What the Turtles Know
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She takes Theo on her nest survey; he watches her work with the island's volunteers and sees who she's become. He admits his career collapsed after the record deal. Emotional beat: guarded honesty, admiration breaking through resentment.

chapters.title: Power Out, Walls Down
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A second storm night, candles and canned chili. He tells her the truth he's never told anyone: he left because her father paid him to, believing it would save her from his failures. Emotional beat: devastation and the first real exhale of ten years.

chapters.title: The Wrong Kind of Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Reeling from Theo's revelation, she rages at her dead father's interference — and at Theo for letting her believe she was unlovable. She walks out into the snow. Emotional beat: anger as the last wall before grief.

chapters.title: Snowbound Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo finds her at the beach in the impossible snow; they finally say everything, including that they never stopped loving each other. They kiss as the storm breaks. Emotional beat: catharsis, ten years of silence ending in one night.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Ferry service resumes; reality returns with the ice melting. The Monterey grant — the career that saved her — requires her presence in California within two weeks. Emotional beat: joy shadowed immediately by the ticking clock.

chapters.title: Two Weeks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He stays on the island, helping with hatchling season, writing again for the first time in years. They fall into a rhythm that feels dangerously like the life they might have had. Emotional beat: stolen happiness, both refusing to name the deadline.

chapters.title: The Offer on the Table
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The grant committee calls: the Monterey directorship is hers, permanent, starting next month — contingent on her relocation. Theo says she should take it. She can't tell if he means it. Emotional beat: love tested by generosity that feels like retreat.

chapters.title: The Gig He Missed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His Mobile reschedule finally happens; Zephyrine drives him. Onstage he debuts a new song — 'Brightwater' — written for her. She realizes he's asking her to stay without saying it. Emotional beat: public vulnerability, love made audible.

chapters.title: Old Ghosts, New Arguments
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Her father's old business partner surfaces, revealing her father left her a letter she never received — his apology, and his blessing to choose her own life. Emotional beat: grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Monterey Calling
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She flies to California for the final interview and is offered everything she built her second life around. Walking the aquarium at night, she realizes the career didn't save her — she did, and she can bring that self anywhere. Emotional beat: clarity, agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Empty Nest
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Back on the island, he prepares to leave, believing she'll choose Monterey and a life without him. He packs the songbook she left behind and writes a final page. Emotional beat: heartbreak mistaken for maturity.

chapters.title: The Letter She Never Read
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She returns to the island to find Theo's note and her father's letter together. Her father wrote that he was wrong, that love isn't a debt to be paid by sacrifice. She runs for the dock as Theo's ferry pulls away. Emotional beat: desperation, the arc's lowest point.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A squall delays the ferry; Theo's boat turns back. They meet on the dock in the rain, both having chosen wrong for the right reasons. They finally negotiate honestly: no more sacrifices made in secret. Emotional beat: collision, then stillness.

chapters.title: Terms of Belonging
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She counters the committee: she'll take the directorship as a hybrid post, splitting time between Monterey and Pelican Key, building a Gulf satellite program. Theo proposes coming with her — not following her, joining her. Emotional beat: love redesigned rather than renounced.

chapters.title: The Song He Should Have Written
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Hatchling night: hundreds of turtles make for the sea under a full moon. Theo plays 'Brightwater' complete at last, with the verse he couldn't write until now — about coming back. Emotional beat: fullness, the found family of volunteers singing along.

chapters.title: Dawn Census
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Final chapter mirrors the first: the dawn survey, but now Theo walks beside her, and the count includes a new nest — and a new plan. She still counts turtles, but no longer instead of heartbreaks. Emotional beat: belonging, memory made peace with, a beginning disguised as an ending.
